In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible interactions of the benzodiazepines and the endorphin system.
the possible role of the endogenous opiates as regulators of the GABA-benzodiazepine-chloride ionophore system in the central nervous system.
the development of a new class of benzodiazepines that are selective for the benzodiazepinic binding site on the GABA receptor complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the benzodiazepines are the most important drugs for the treatment of anxiety.
the MIF-1 family of peptides has no direct interaction with the benzodiazepinic binding site, but rather interacts with the GABA receptor.
the MIF-1 peptides are benzodiazepinic and/or GABAergic in nature, but not opioidergic, and that they may be useful in the study of the GABA-opiate receptor interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the endogenous opiopeptide system may modulate the benzodiazepines' actions at benzodiazepinergic receptors.
benzodiazepines and GABA have a synergistic effect on benzodiazpene receptor binding.
Tyr-MIF- 1 is the most potent benzodiazepinic peptide known and that it has a unique ability to augment GABA-stimulation of benzodiazepines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the endogenous opioid antagonist MIF-1 can modulate benzodiazepines.
MIF-1 (and Tyr-MIF- 1) is a GABAergic peptide that augments GABA-stimulate benzodiazepines receptor binding.
the benzodiazepines are not the only drugs that bind to the benzodiazepam receptor.
